cards.explanation: The answer is that they offer to serve him under a treaty. The men of Jabesh say, “Make a treaty with us, and we will serve you.” Nahash has laid siege to their town, friends, and that's the offer they bring him.

The answer is all Israel. Nahash the Ammonite says he'll do it “…and bring reproach upon all Israel.” So it's bigger than one town under siege. This part is heavy, friends, and I think the elders felt the weight of it.

The answer is False. The elders of Jabesh don't take his condition. They say, “Hold off for seven days…” and ask to send messengers throughout Israel. They aren't ready to say yes yet, and I'd want a few days to look for help too.

The answer is True, and the elders say it plainly: “If there is no one to save us, we will surrender to you.” The seven days are a window, friends. They're looking for a rescuer, and the surrender is what happens if none shows up.

The answer is wept. When the messengers relay the words from Jabesh in the hearing of the people, they “wept aloud.” The whole crowd breaks down, friends. It was the kind of news that stops a town in its tracks.

The answer is the Spirit of God. The text says, “…the Spirit of God rushed upon him…” Saul has just come back from the field behind his oxen, and the news from Jabesh reaches him. Then the Spirit rushes upon him, and the text says he burned with great anger.
The answer is anger. Saul “…burned with great anger.” The people around him are weeping, and Saul is burning. The text doesn't tell us more than that, friends, about what's going on inside him.

The answer is march behind Saul and Samuel or else, and the words are strong. Saul sends the pieces out saying, “This is what will be done to the oxen of anyone who does not march behind Saul and Samuel.” Samuel is Israel's prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), and Saul puts his name right next to his own. Pieces of oxen are hard to ignore, friends.
The answer is False, because it's no small crowd. At Bezek, Saul numbers 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah. I'd have needed a bigger counting table, friends.

The answer is tomorrow by the time the sun is hot. The messengers carry this promise home: “Deliverance will be yours tomorrow by the time the sun is hot.” That's a short wait, friends. And when the messengers relay it, the men of Jabesh rejoice.

The answer is that tomorrow they'll come out to him. The men of Jabesh tell Nahash, “Tomorrow we will come out…” and add that he can do with them whatever seems good to him. Their words to him are about coming out, friends. They say nothing yet about help on the way.

The answer is True. The survivors were “…so scattered that no two of them were left together.” This is a heavy part of the story, friends, and the text tells it plainly. The Ammonite camp is completely broken up.

The answer is to put them to death, and the people say it outright: “Bring those men here so we can kill them!” They have just asked, “Who said that Saul should not reign over us?” and the men they mean are the ones who said it. That's a heavy thing to say, friends, and Saul answers it next.

The answer is False. Saul does not agree with them. He orders, “No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.” The people ask for one thing and Saul orders another. It's a heavy moment, friends, and Saul's answer points to the LORD.

The answer is the LORD. Saul says, “…for today the LORD has worked salvation in Israel.” Saul had just led the army, friends, and he points to the LORD for the salvation. That's what he says in front of everybody.

The answer is Gilgal. Samuel says, “Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingship there.” Samuel is Israel's prophet (1 Samuel 3:20), and he's the one leading the way. The people follow him there in verse 15, friends.

The answer is rejoice. The text says that after the peace offerings before the LORD, “…Saul and all the Israelites rejoiced greatly.” It's a big celebration after everything in this passage, friends. Rejoicing greatly is exactly how it ends.
